# Corridor distance tables lifted verbatim from the JARAK ANTAR STASIUN
# section of "Train Timetables/GAPEKA Jadwal Kereta.pdf", exactly as
# pdfplumber's extract_text() yields them, except that trailing whitespace is
# stripped. The PDF takes ~9 minutes to extract, so no test may open it.
#
# tests/conftest.py groups these by the "# page N" markers and drops comments
# and blank lines. No register line starts with '#', so nothing is lost.
#
# Seven pages, each chosen for one quirk:
#
#   52  a clean header row, and the short branches printed as inline pairs
#       ("BPR - BST 12,300 KEN-CGD 6,439") on the same line as a code route.
#   53  two corridors that share both of their ends, Jakarta Kota to Cikampek
#       by Pasar Senen and by Manggarai, which only print order tells apart.
#       Also inline pairs tucked onto the end of an index row and onto the end
#       of a matrix row, where they must not be read as distances.
#   54  the first block only: an inline pair on a line of its own, and a code
#       route, "KPB-DU-THB-MRI", that runs one station further than the matrix
#       below it does, so naming a corridor on the head code alone would have
#       it claim a station it has no distance for.
#   55  the header arriving interleaved ("O/D C 1KP C 2BR PW 3K ..."), four
#       corridors on one page, two of them printed side by side, and the
#       vertical-text wreckage that costs the Padalarang - Sukabumi corridor
#       its 7th and 8th rows.
#   58  two lines of the same wreckage, from where the Banjar - Kroya matrix
#       should have its 8th, 9th, 11th and 12th rows. These two lines only,
#       not the whole page: everything a parser can get wrong about them is in
#       them, and a comma-less number is all that stands between "GL 98 76"
#       and a station called GL at km 76.
#   62  two tables printed side by side, one text line holding a row from each.
#       Only the first block of the page is here; page 62 continues with a
#       third, unrelated matrix (Wlingi - Surabaya Pasarturi), which would make
#       the side-by-side count three and says nothing new about splitting.
#   63  the whole Ketapang - Bangil page, whose matrix prints some cells to one
#       or two decimals where row 1 of the same matrix gives three, so a cell
#       has to be matched at the precision the register printed it.
